header: Problem 4 Phosphoric Acid and Phosphate Chemistry. Phosphates are important in industrial production, food additives, and other fields, so measuring their content and understanding their properties are significant.

subquestions.text_open: 4-1 Aqueous sodium phosphate dodecahydrate, Na_3PO_4·12H_2O, is strongly basic and is used in washing powders and fat-saponification agents. It is prepared by reacting calcium dihydrogen phosphate with sodium carbonate and then adding sodium hydroxide solution. Write the preparation equation.

Titration notation: Add a volume $V_0$ of standard HCl of concentration $c_1$ to the sample, then titrate with standard NaOH of concentration $c_2$. The first jump near pH 4.0 consumes a NaOH volume $V_1$, and continuing to the second jump near pH 8.8 consumes an additional volume $V_2$.
4-2-2 What relation among V_0, V_1, V_2, c_1, and c_2 indicates that the sample contains Na_2HPO_4? Express it symbolically.
4-2-3 Calculate the mass fraction ω(%) of Na_3PO_4 in the sample. Significant figures are required.
rubric: First determine that $30 × 1.057 - 9.60 × 1.032 < 2 × 10.75 × 1.032$, showing that the sample contains Na_2HPO_4. (2 points)

$\omega =\frac{30.00\times 1.057-9.60\times 1.032-10.75\times 1.032\times {{10}^{-3}}\times 163.94}{2.013}=87.22\%$. (2 points; directly obtaining n(Na_3PO_4) = 0.01071 mol without the determination also earns 2 points. Deduct 1 point for incorrect significant figures.)

subquestions.text_open: 4-3-2 Phosphorus atoms in different oxidation states can also be linked in catenated phosphoric acids. H_4P_2O_5 contains linked P(Ⅱ) and P(Ⅳ). It has two hydrolysis pathways under basic conditions. Only the first generates gas, and each gives only one phosphorus-containing product. Write the ionic equations for both pathways.
rubric: Writing reactants or products in acid form earns 1 point per equation. Answers containing (P_2O_5)^(4-) or (PO_3)^(3-) receive no credit.

subquestions.text_open: 4-3-3 Hydrolysis of cyclic H_6P_6O_12 is complex. First, one P-P bond cleaves to form a linear catenated hexaphosphoric acid by disproportionation; then terminal P-P bonds cleave stepwise. How many ways can the linear hexaphosphoric acid hydrolyze to catenated pentaphosphoric acid? Give the products of each. Use P for a phosphorus-containing group and a superscript to denote oxidation state; for example, catenated diphosphoric acid is P^4-P^4.
rubric: Deduct 1 point for an incorrect hydrolysis pathway and 1 point if the monophosphorus product is omitted.
